name: Phylactery
overview: The phylactery, a small box containing parchment slips with portions of God's law, served as a visible and tangible reminder of His commandments, worn by the Jews on the head and left arm as described in Exodus 13:9,16. These passages emphasize the importance of keeping God's law always before the believer, symbolized by the placement 'upon thine hand' and 'between thine eyes,' reflecting wholehearted love and devotion to the one true Lord (Deuteronomy 6:4-5). The law was to be internalized and diligently taught within the home and daily life (Deuteronomy 6:6-7), underscoring the call to live in constant remembrance and obedience to God’s covenant.
